official_assessment: Northern adult ILI rose abruptly; H1N1 outbreaks were multi-province.
evidence_note: Northern adult ILI% rose 1.5% to 2.4%, above the prior two surveillance-year peaks; 48 H1N1 outbreaks were reported in 13 provinces. H1N1 was 211 positives and 9.5% of all influenza positives.

official_assessment: ILI rose in southern and northern adult/paediatric clinics, with marked pathogen-specific expansion.
evidence_note: H1N1 positives increased to 525 and 20.5% of all influenza positives; 102 H1N1 outbreaks and 3,955 confirmed cases were reported; ILI rose in all four monitored clinic strata.

official_assessment: ILI and pathogen-specific/geographic spread continued to rise.
evidence_note: H1N1 was 801 positives (32.3% of influenza A positives); 104 H1N1 outbreaks occurred in 24 provinces, 63 cities and 84 counties. The 31.6% figure is total influenza positivity and is not treated as H1N1-specific evidence.

official_assessment: Low activity nationally; only individual southern provinces were rising.
evidence_note: Sixteen ILI outbreaks were reported; the national summary did not yet describe region-wide southern activity as rising.

official_assessment: Low activity nationally; only individual southern provinces were rising.
evidence_note: Eleven ILI outbreaks were reported; the official category remained low/localised.

official_assessment: Southern-province influenza activity was reported as rising; northern activity remained low.
evidence_note: This is the first reviewed week in which the official assessment escalated from individual southern provinces to the southern-province region. Four ILI outbreaks were reported.

official_assessment: Southern-province activity remained rising; outbreak burden increased.
evidence_note: The regional assessment persisted and reported ILI outbreaks rose from 4 to 49, providing an independent quantitative confirmation stream.

official_assessment: Southern activity continued rising and activity rose in some northern provinces.
evidence_note: Expansion persisted and broadened geographically; 144 ILI outbreaks were reported.
